description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:160-162

```rust
pub const fn new(logs: CtLogList, verifier: V) -> Self {
    Self { logs, verifier }
}
```

The `const fn` qualifier commits the maintainer to a body that is
const-evaluable forever. Any future version that wants to:

- Validate `logs` (reject empty list, check for duplicate log_ids
  across operators)
- Pre-compute a `log_id -> SPKI` cache to avoid re-parsing on every
  verify call
- Lazily wire in algorithm-pref ordering

…is now blocked, because none of those can be `const fn` until
`Vec::new()` and `BTreeMap::iter()` are stably const in Rust, which
they are not.

`const fn` was the right answer for a zero-cost wrapper; it is the
wrong answer if validation or pre-computation belongs in the
constructor. The maintainer paid forward an optimization (callable
in const contexts) that no real caller will use, and locked future
flexibility.

Recommendation: drop `const` from `new`. Callers cannot tell the
difference; removing const is a non-breaking change so this can be
done at any 0.x release, but if it's wrong it's wrong to leave it.

Same critique applies to `CtLogList::new` (line 64) and
`SctVerifier::logs` (line 166): the latter two are pure accessors and
const is fine there; only `SctVerifier::new` carries forward
construction-time validation potential.

Marking P3 because const can be dropped silently as a non-breaking
change; this is just preventative.
title: SctVerifier::new is const fn — locks construction shape across versions
